header:
Meeting: Console walkthrough - Usage analytics & per-route cost breakdown
Date: 2025-06-10
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Nina Patel (Head of ML, ParcelCloud), Roberto Diaz (Platform Eng, ParcelCloud), Ellen Cho (CTO, ParcelCloud)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. this is Maya from Redwood, I'll kick us off — quick agenda: show the console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and the cost breakdown features then Q&A. Diego will do the deep-dive on the per-route metrics.
[00:18] Nina: Great, thanks. we're really interested in how we'd map our microservices to routes and understand token cost per endpoint.
[00:28] Diego: Yeah, absolutely. so first screen, this is the usage overview, you can filter by time range, model, and route. uh, note that we surface token-level breakdowns so you can see prompt vs completion tokens and the unit cost per token.
[00:45] Roberto: Quick question, are those unit costs pre-populated or do we put our committed pricing?
[00:52] Maya: Good question — for hosted accounts we show Redwood list pricing and an estimated cost; for dedicated/reserved customers you can upload or configure your contract pricing and the console will apply it to the token usage so you get accurate billing predictions.
[01:10] Diego: jumping to per-route dashboards now — each route maps to a path or API key in your app. here we show request volume, p50/p95 latency, tokens per request histogram, and a cost column. you can pivot by model, region, and customer tag.
[01:32] Ellen: Can we group routes into logical services? our billing needs are org-level so we want to aggregate many endpoints.
[01:38] Diego: yes, you can create a "route group" or use tags. we also have a feature to auto-suggest grouping based on request patterns — it tries to match prefixes and headers. (murmur) it's, uh, helpful for large apps.
[01:55] Nina: The anomaly detection — does it alert on cost spikes?
[01:58] Diego: it does. there's a cost-monitor setting: set thresholds on absolute token spend or percent delta week-over-week. alerts can post to Slack, email, or our webhook. we also keep 90-day retention in advanced plans, longer if you request it.
[02:15] Roberto: about KMS/encryption — will the console show decrypted payloads? we need to make sure PII isn't logged.
[02:22] Maya: No — by default the transcript/preview in the console is redacted. raw payloads are not stored unless you opt in and sign a data retention addendum. we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM for Private deployments.
[02:40] Diego: now the cost breakdown view — you can pick a time window and it breaks down cost by model, by route, and by customer tag. it also shows the effect of batching and caching on effective tokens billed. so for example if you have KV cache hits we subtract those from billed tokens in the chart (note: small transcription error earlier — we say K-V cache sometimes as K V cache).
[03:05] Nina: do you show model variants? like gpt-like 13b quantized vs full precision?
[03:10] Diego: yes, we show model variant columns. when you run a rollout you can compare cost/latency/quality across variants in the same dashboard. this is helpful if you want to canary a quantized variant to save cost.
[03:25] Maya: and the rollout integration ties to the routing policies — if the canary exceeds a latency SLO we automatically fallback to the stable variant, and the dashboard shows the fallback rate.
[03:37] Roberto: any autocomplete or misnamed model issues? sometimes open-source names get fuzzy.
[03:41] Diego: the console attempts to normalize model names and tags them with architecture and quantization level but yeah occasionally the auto-detect mislabels a fork. you can manually override name/alias.
[03:54] Nina: what's the granularity of the per-route cost? is it per request or per minute aggregated?
[03:59] Diego: billed cost is computed per request then aggregated for charts. we store per-request metadata for up to the retention window you select; default is 30 days on hosted.
[04:15] Ellen: for the POC we want to simulate 50k reqs/day across 10 routes. will the console forecast cost?
[04:21] Maya: yep, in the cost simulator set traffic profile, choose batching settings and quantization, and it'll give you a projected spend and per-route breakdown. we'll include that in the pricing doc.
[04:35] (30s silence/Filler)
[04:40] Diego: demoing the trace view — click into a slow route and you can see token timelines, KV cache hit markers, GPU queuing time, and which model/kernels were used. this helps debug which layer is causing latency.
[05:02] Roberto: GPU queuing — do you show queue depth per instance?
[05:06] Diego: yes, per-pod queue depth. for dedicated customers we can also surface per-shard metrics.
[05:15] Nina: security/compliance — we need SOC2 and SAML SSO.
[05:19] Maya: we've got SOC 2 Type II and SAML/SCIM SSO; dashboard has RBAC roles and audit logs for all console actions. we'll share the security pack after this meeting.
[05:33] Nina: are audit logs exportable?
[05:35] Maya: yes, you can export as JSON or stream to your SIEM via syslog or our webhook.
[05:41] Diego: quick note about cost attribution — if you use our caching layer there is a small infra cost but it often reduces overall token spend by >20% for chat-heavy workloads. the console shows net savings in the optimization tab.
[05:58] Ellen: any examples or benchmarks you can share?
[06:02] Maya: we'll send a benchmark sheet — we've got examples for ecomm search, support chat, and personalization workloads.
[06:12] Nina: on routing policies — can we route by customer tier? like paid traffic goes to dedicated pool, free traffic to hosted with lower SLOs?
[06:19] Diego: yes that's a common pattern — route by header or API key to different pools. the console shows cross-pool aggregated views as well.
[06:30] (minute jump)
[07:00] Diego: opening the Optimize tab — suggestions engine will recommend batching window and quantization level per route based on latency tolerance and quality thresholds you provide. it simulates the cost/latency tradeoff.
[07:20] Roberto: do suggestions apply automatically or just recommendations?
[07:23] Diego: recommendations only; you can apply them with one click but we require confirmation and a canary rollout.
[07:35] Nina: about the per-token breakdown in the UI — is it possible to export CSV with token counts per request?
[07:40] Diego: yes exportable per request, also aggregated summaries.
[07:45] Ellen: any gotchas for private/on-prem installs? we have strict network policies.
[07:50] Maya: for Private we deploy a control plane in your VPC; console traffic can be regionalized and audit logs stay within your network if you choose. KMS integration is supported.
[08:05] (small crosstalk)
[08:15] Nina: what's the expected timeline to go from POC to production if the POC looks good?
[08:20] Maya: typically 6-8 weeks for a medium integration: POC (2-3 weeks), validate quality and cost, then migration plan for Dedicated or Private if needed. depends on compliance ops.
[08:33] Diego: another small demo — here's the per-route cost waterfall: model cost, infra surcharge, and caching savings. you can toggle to show "effective cost per 1k requests" which many FinOps teams like.
[08:50] Nina: neat. can you also show per-team cost allocation? we want to chargeback.
[08:55] Diego: yep tags -> allocation reports; you can schedule monthly exports for chargeback to billing.
[09:05] (fast-forward)
[20:00] Diego: jumping ahead to Q&A — (paraphrase) someone asked about integration with our monitoring stack; yes, we have OpenTelemetry traces and metrics exporters.
[20:20] Roberto: do you support custom metrics? e.g., quality metric from our evals?
[20:24] Diego: you can upload your evals or link to an eval set and we surface quality deltas tied to a route's prompts. the console will flag regressions post-rollout.
[21:00] Nina: any limitations on retention for per-request telemetry on hosted?
[21:04] Maya: default 30 days; you can purchase extended retention up to 13 months depending on plan. Private deployments can set retention per your policies.
[22:10] Ellen: okay let's talk deliverables.
[22:14] Maya: recap — we'll send: detailed pricing/cost model with POC simulator, console recording and dashboard links, SOC2 and security pack, and a simple onboarding checklist.
[22:26] Nina: great. Diego, can you share the specific dashboards for route-grouping and the anomaly config?
[22:31] Diego: yes i'll export them and share.
[22:35] Maya: next steps: we'll schedule the POC kickoff for week of 2025-06-16, target 50k reqs/day simulation.
[22:43] (wrap)
[22:45] Maya: any final Qs?
[22:47] Roberto: none from me, looks good.
[22:49] Nina: thanks, appreciate the walkthrough.
[22:51] Maya: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with artifacts. bye.

Summary: Quick console demo focusing on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, cost breakdown, rollout/optimize features, and security/compliance. Customer wants a POC (50k reqs/day) with detailed cost model. Action items and next steps agreed.
